claims: "Taco Tuesday Trump" refers to the acronym TACO (Trump Always Chickens Out).
Financial Times columnist Robert Armstrong coined the term TACO in May 2025.
Robert Armstrong coined TACO to describe a pattern during Donald Trump's second term.
The term TACO originated on Wall Street to describe a "TACO trade".
A "TACO trade" is a strategy of investing based on the expectation that Trump's aggressive trade threats will be reversed, leading to a market surge.
The phrase gained traction during threatened tariff hikes on the European Union and Mexico.
The phrase gained traction when military threats regarding Iran were followed by negotiations.
Democratic groups parked a taco truck with images of Trump in a chicken suit outside the Republican National Committee headquarters to protest tariff policies.
Trump argued that his actions are a calculated negotiation tactic, not a "chicken out".
Trump cited his ability to force foreign nations to negotiate.
TACO Tuesday references the day of the week these policy reversals or protests often occur.
